cleanIntro: Henry's H015 shotgun book. A break-action single shot with a rebounding hammer and an interlock instead of a manual safety — and a genuine published field strip: knock the barrel pivot pin out and the barrel comes off the frame. Page numbers here are the printed folios, which do not track the PDF pages.

steps.title: Hammer down first — the interlock will not let the action open otherwise
steps.action: Before anything else, make sure the hammer is not cocked. Henry's interlock will not let the action open OR close while the hammer is cocked, so a cocked hammer is not a stiff action, it is a locked one. If the release lever will not move, drop the hammer under control rather than forcing the lever.
steps.quote: Be sure the hammer on your firearm is not cocked. Henry's interlock system does not allow the action to open or close if the hammer is cocked.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO LOAD YOUR HENRY SINGLE SHOT SHOTGUN, p.8

steps.title: Release lever pivoted, barrel broken open
steps.action: Pivot the locking release lever on the top of the frame, behind the hammer spur, to either side — it works left or right, so use whichever hand suits you. The barrel then swings down on its hinge and exposes the breech. Support the barrel as it drops rather than letting it fall open against its stop.
steps.quote: Your break-action firearm uses a locking release lever on top of the frame, behind the external hammer spur to break open for loading and unloading.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO LOAD YOUR HENRY SINGLE SHOT SHOTGUN, p.9

steps.title: Breech checked, shell or hull accounted for
steps.action: With the action open, look into the chamber and confirm it is empty. This gun ejects the fired hull fully when it is opened after firing, so an unfired shell behaves differently from a spent one — do not assume that because nothing flew out, nothing is in there. Check with your eyes on the chamber.
steps.aside: As with loading, be sure the hammer on your firearm is not cocked. Henry's interlock system does not allow the action to open if the hammer is cocked.
steps.quote: The H015 single shot shotgun fully ejects the shotgun shell/hull after firing.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD YOUR HENRY SINGLE SHOT SHOTGUN, p.9

steps.title: Shotgun confirmed unloaded, muzzle safe, ammunition away
steps.action: Confirm the shotgun is completely unloaded and keep the muzzle in a safe direction for the rest of the job. Move the shells out of the cleaning area first. Henry also wants the hammer down so the rebounding hammer safety is working as designed while you handle the gun.
steps.quote: MAKE CERTAIN YOUR SHOTGUN IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED. KEEP THE MUZZLE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — CLEANING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, p.11
steps.warn: KEEP ALL AMMUNITION AWAY FROM THE CLEANING AREA. NEVER TEST THE MECHANICAL FUNCTION OF YOUR SHOTGUN WITH LIVE AMMUNITION.

steps.title: Clean the chamber promptly after plastic shotshells
steps.action: Do not leave a fired hull sitting in the chamber and do not put the gun away dirty. Henry warns that plastic shotshells hold moisture that sweats out onto the chamber wall and corrodes it. On a single shot the chamber is also the breech face you are looking at every time you load, so pitting there is both a rust problem and an extraction problem.
steps.quote: NOTICE! It is very important that the chambers of your shotgun be cleaned thoroughly and promptly after shooting plastic shotshells.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — CLEANING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, p.11

steps.title: Hammer at rest, action opened, chamber verified empty
steps.action: Henry's field strip opens with its own clearing check: hammer in the resting position, action open, chamber confirmed empty. Do it again here even though you cleared the gun earlier — you are about to drive a pin out of the frame, and this is the last point at which a shell in the chamber is still a recoverable mistake.
steps.quote: 1) With the hammer in the resting position, open the action to verify that the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — FIELD STRIPPING YOUR HENRY H015 SINGLE SHOT RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, step 1, p.12

steps.title: Barrel pivot pin tapped out with a soft dowel
steps.action: Drive the pivot pin out with a 3/8 inch or smaller dowel or rod of wood, brass or plastic — soft materials only, and it can go either direction. A steel punch on this pin will burr the pin and mark the frame around the hole. Tap it, do not hammer it: the pin is a slip fit, not an interference fit.
steps.quote: 2) Remove the pivot pin by tapping it out with a 3/8" diameter or smaller wooden, brass, or plastic dowel or rod. This can be done from either direction.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — FIELD STRIPPING YOUR HENRY H015 SINGLE SHOT RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, step 2, p.12

steps.title: Barrel assembly lifted off the receiver
steps.action: Lift the barrel assembly off the receiver. Watch the ejector/extractor release pin as it goes — it has to pass cleanly through the slots in either side of the receiver, so let the barrel come away square rather than twisting it. If it snags, back it up and realign instead of pulling harder; that pin is what makes the gun eject.
steps.prose: Be sure your Single Shot is unloaded. Remove the barrel pivot pin by tapping it out (in either direction). Remove the barrel from the frame.
steps.quote: 3) Remove the barrel assembly from the receiver assembly. The ejector/extractor release pin needs to pass cleanly through the slots in either side of the receiver.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — FIELD STRIPPING YOUR HENRY H015 SINGLE SHOT RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, step 3, p.12

steps.title: Bore cleaned breech to muzzle with the choke tube fitted
steps.action: With the barrel off you have a clear straight run at the bore. Clean from the breech toward the muzzle, following the shot. Leave a choke tube installed while you do it — Henry is specific about this, because cleaning an empty choke thread packs residue into the threads where it sets hard and seizes the next tube.
steps.caution: During cleaning of the barrel, be certain a choke tube is properly installed.
steps.quote: Using a brand name cleaning kit, run the cleaning rod down the bore from the breech towards the muzzle. ALWAYS CLEAN FROM THE NATURAL DIRECTION OF THE BULLET.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY SHOTGUN, p.12

steps.title: Choke threads kept clean and lightly oiled
steps.action: Keep the precision threads on the choke tube clean and lightly oiled at all times. Check the tube is still tight periodically — a choke that backs out under recoil damages both the tube and the barrel threads. And never fire the gun with no tube in place at all; the threads take the blast directly and are ruined.
steps.quote: The precision threads on your choke tube should be kept clean and lightly oiled at all times. During cleaning of the barrel, be certain a choke tube is properly installed.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — CARE & CLEANING, p.10
steps.warn: NEVER FIRE YOUR SHOTGUN WITHOUT A CHOKE IN PLACE. FIRING WITHOUT A CHOKE CAN DAMAGE THE THREADS FOR THE CHOKE.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel assembly, pivot pin and receiver are separated — that is Henry's published strip for this shotgun, and the manual is clear you do not have to go this far just to clean it. Reassembly is the reverse, and Henry attaches a functional check to it rather than leaving it implied. Nothing deeper is published for the owner.
steps.quote: To reassemble, reverse these steps, making sure that you check for proper functioning of the action, hammer, and trigger mechanisms prior to loading and firing.
steps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — FIELD STRIPPING YOUR HENRY H015 SINGLE SHOT RIFLE OR SHOTGUN, p.12

deepSteps.title: Choke tube out with the supplied wrench
deepSteps.action: Open the action and verify the gun is unloaded first, then fit the supplied wrench so its stepped end engages the notches in the choke tube and turn counter-clockwise. Once it is loose take it out with your fingers and set it on a clean dry surface. Inspect it before it goes anywhere near the barrel again — a dented or deformed threaded end will damage the barrel threads.
deepSteps.quote: To change or remove the choke tubes, use the wrench that was supplied.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — REMOVAL OF CHOKE TUBES, p.9
deepSteps.warn: MAKE SURE TO INSPECT CHOKES FOR DAMAGE BEFORE INSTALLATION AS A DAMAGED CHOKE MAY DAMAGE YOUR SHOTGUN AND/OR CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY.

deepSteps.title: Frame, breech face and hinge wiped down with the barrel off
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off, the frame is as open as it will ever be — wipe the breech face, the hinge and the pivot pin bore clean and re-oil lightly. This is the payoff for stripping it. Do not go further: Henry stops the owner procedure here and the hammer and trigger mechanism inside the frame are not an owner-level assembly.
deepSteps.prose: If further disassembly for service or cleaning is required, take your firearm to a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: NOTICE! DO NOT ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS MANUAL.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — FIELD STRIPPING YOUR SINGLE SHOT SHOTGUN, p.12

deepSteps.title: Assembled cleaning is enough for routine work
deepSteps.action: Worth knowing for next time: Henry says outright that this shotgun does not have to be disassembled to be cleaned properly. Breaking the action open gives access to the chamber and the bore from the breech end, which covers ordinary use. Save the pivot-pin strip for when the gun has actually been wet or heavily fouled.
deepSteps.quote: You do not have to disassemble this shotgun in order to clean it sufficiently and to keep it operating properly.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H015 Shotgun Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY SHOTGUN, p.13

cleaning.name: BORE & CHOKE
tasks: Clean the bore breech to muzzle with a choke tube installed
Remove the tube afterwards, wipe the threads in the barrel and on the tube, oil lightly
Check the tube seats flush with the muzzle and is tight before firing

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & BREECH
tasks: Clean the chamber promptly — plastic hulls sweat moisture onto it
Wipe the breech face and the extractor/ejector cutout
Check the extractor moves freely in the barrel face

cleaning.name: FRAME & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the hinge, pivot pin and pin bore, then oil lightly
Wipe the release lever and around the hammer spur
Film of oil on exposed steel; wipe brass-framed models with a dry cloth

reassembly: Offer the barrel assembly up to the receiver, letting the ejector/extractor release pin pass cleanly through the receiver slots.
Line the pivot holes up and tap the pivot pin back through with the same soft dowel.
Close the action and confirm the release lever returns to its centre position and locks.
Check for proper functioning of the action, hammer, and trigger mechanisms prior to loading and firing.
fncheck: With the shotgun confirmed empty, check that the action opens and closes only with the hammer down, that the release lever locks the barrel positively when closed, that the hammer rebounds off the firing pin when lowered, and that the extractor lifts a dummy or empty hull cleanly.
